title: Maple Leaf Rag and the Red Back Book
summary: Ridgley says Tuxedo played little Maple Leaf Rag, which belonged to earlier players, and that Billy Marrero's Superior band used the Red Back Book. Newer bands change the tune.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Well, what about something like Maple Leaf Rag? Would you have a key change in that?

Well, Maple Leaf Rag, I'll tell you back at that time, it wasn't everybody who could play Maple Leaf Rag. I was wondering if we'd play on it, but, and so we just used to play it just like it was. But you see, since my time, they do all of that now. They make those changes. But we didn't do it back then, you know. Did you? We didn't have that in mind. Did you have that Redback book?
Redback, no. You didn't use that for playing Rag then?

We didn't have that. You know, Maple Leaf Rag, before my time, that was an old number. And they used to play it a whole lot before my time. But we didn't play too much of Maple Leaf Rag in our time, but they're playing it plenty since I quit. You see those fellas? And those fellas like rearranging those things now, they don't carry on Maple Leaf, they don't carry on it the same way. If you wouldn't know something about it you wouldn't know it was Maple Leaf Rag. They didn't tour it up now.
Do you remember the Siberia band that Billy Moran had?
Yeah, sure, bass player Billy Moran.
Well in a band like that they played the Redback book plenty, I hear.
They had a good clarinet player for them red-back books.
Maple Leaf Rag, any kind of clarinet player couldn't believe. Not from their book.
So the Tuxedo didn't use that much, those kind of numbers?
Not many. We didn't use that kind of numbers.
But they had plenty of changes of key in that.

Oh, you don't play any. They didn't have any proof of that much. But we couldn't play it. We played it from the, you know, Auguste Frasin. Played like that. But we never did proof of Maple Leaf very much. Not too much. In our time we had so much other things, you see, like the records was coming out and all like that, you know. We used plenty of other fellas' records.
